CV.extension: The visa exemption cannot be extended in-country: the government portal directs anyone who wants to stay beyond the exemption period to apply for a visa at the nearest Cabo Verdean embassy or consular post.
CV.overstay: No official overstay tariff is published in the sources used here — leave within the stay you were granted, or hold a visa that covers the extra time.

documents: EASE pre-registration confirmation, with the TSA paid
routes.fee: No visa fee. Airport security tax (TSA): 3,400 CVE (≈ €31), paid online with the pre-registration. Since 1 July 2026, travellers who arrive without proof of pre-registration pay double the TSA at the border
routes.name: Visa-free entry — with EASE pre-registration
routes.processing: Pre-register on the EASE portal and pay the TSA up to five days before arrival
routes.stay: 30 days for most nationalities; 60 days for Russia and São Tomé and Príncipe; 90 days for ECOWAS members, Macau and South Korea; 180 days for Angola, Guinea-Bissau, Mozambique and Ukraine — per the official table
routes.who: Nationals of the 67 countries on the government's exempt list, including the United Kingdom, the United States, EU member states, China and ECOWAS members. Find your passport in the status table below.

documents: EASE pre-registration confirmation, with the TSA paid
routes.fee: Cabo Verde publishes no consolidated border-visa fee in the sources used here — confirm at the border. The airport security tax (TSA, 3,400 CVE online; doubled at the border since 1 July 2026 without proof of pre-registration) applies to all travellers
routes.name: Visa on arrival (Visto de Fronteira)
routes.processing: EASE pre-registration before travel; the visa itself is issued on arrival
routes.stay: Set by the visa issued at the border — Cabo Verde publishes no consolidated maximum stay for this channel
routes.who: Travellers whose nationality is on neither the exempt list nor the Interior Ministry's pre-arrival-visa list (Despacho n.º 244/GMAI/2026, in force since 1 January 2026). The visa is issued at Cabo Verde's international airports and seaports.

documents: As listed by the embassy or consulate (application form, photo, passport, trip evidence)
routes.fee: Charged by the embassy or consulate — confirm the current amount with it
routes.name: Visa before travel (embassy or consulate)
routes.who: Nationalities named in Despacho n.º 244/GMAI/2026 must hold a visa before arrival. Visa-exempt nationals who want to stay beyond the exemption period must also apply at a Cabo Verdean embassy or consulate — that is the route the government portal itself gives for longer stays.

sources.name: Government portal — visa-exempt countries for Cabo Verde

MA.extension: An e-Visa stay cannot be extended, and multiple e-Visas cannot be combined. For visa-free and consular stays, the official sources used here publish no general extension procedure — Law No. 02-03 caps a stay without a residence card at 90 days, so plan to leave within the stay you were granted.
MA.overstay: Staying past your granted period without a residence card breaches Law No. 02-03, which provides for removal from the territory and penalties.

portal.name: Accès Maroc — official e-Visa / AEVM portal

documents: A passport (or other travel document recognised by Morocco) valid for the whole stay
Your passport is stamped on entry; the 90 days run from that stamp
routes.name: Visa-free entry
routes.notes: 90 days is the ceiling Morocco's Law No. 02-03 sets for a stay without a residence card.
routes.processing: No application — entry at the border
routes.who: Nationals of 70 countries, including the United Kingdom, the United States, EU member states, China and Japan. Find your passport in the status table below — the official exemption list is published by Morocco's consular service.

documents: The approved AEVM authorisation — carry it with you when you travel
routes.name: Visa-free with an AEVM authorisation first
routes.processing: Apply on the Accès Maroc portal at least 96 hours before departure
routes.who: Some visa-free nationalities — including Congo-Brazzaville, Ghana and Guinea — must also hold an electronic travel authorisation (AEVM) before travelling. Your pair page in the table below says whether your passport is one of them (Mali's AEVM requirement was lifted on 27 April 2026).

documents: Colour ID photo, 35 × 45 mm, taken within the last 6 months, to ICAO standard
Colour copy of your ordinary passport (identity and validity pages) — passport valid at least 90 days on the day you apply
Category B: colour copy of your residence permit, front and back, valid at least 180 days
Category C: colour copy of the qualifying multiple-entry visa
Business trips: the invitation or recommendation document for the trip
Files must be jpg, jpeg or pdf, at most 1 MB each
routes.fee: The portal shows the fee at checkout — reported as 770 MAD (≈ $78) standard / 1,100 MAD (≈ $112) express, while Morocco's 2025 gazette tariff lists 70 / 100 MAD. The two official figures disagree, so confirm the amount on the portal before you pay. Once paid, the fee is not refunded
routes.name: e-Visa (AEVM portal)
routes.notes: Tourism or business only. An e-Visa cannot be converted into residence, and several e-Visas cannot be combined to stretch a stay — you must leave when the stay on the first one expires. At the border you may also be asked for a return ticket, proof of means (an international bank card or cash worth more than €70 per day of stay) and hospitalisation / repatriation insurance covering the stay.
routes.processing: 72 hours standard / 24 hours express, in Moroccan working days
routes.stay: Single entry; stay up to 30 days. The e-Visa itself is valid up to 180 days from the day it is issued
routes.who: Category A: nationals of Azerbaijan, Benin, Brunei, Cambodia, Guatemala, India, Israel, Jordan, Laos, Thailand and Vietnam. Category B: visa-required nationals holding a residence permit valid at least 180 days from the EU, United States, Australia, Canada, United Kingdom, Japan, Norway, New Zealand, UAE or Switzerland. Category C: holders of a multiple-entry visa valid at least 90 days from Schengen, the United States, Australia, Canada, the United Kingdom, Ireland, Japan, Norway or New Zealand.

documents: The consulate's application form, photo and passport requirements
Evidence for the trip (travel, accommodation and means) as the consulate lists them
routes.fee: Charged by the consulate when you apply — confirm the current amount with it
routes.name: Consular visa (before travel)
routes.notes: If you hold a qualifying residence permit or multiple-entry visa (see the e-Visa route), the online e-Visa is usually the faster path.
routes.processing: Set by the consulate — apply well before travel
routes.stay: Short-stay consular visas are generally up to 90 days; transit visas up to 72 hours
routes.who: Everyone else who needs a visa. Apply at the Moroccan embassy or consulate for your place of residence; there is no general visa on arrival (border-issued visas exist only in exceptional cases, at the border authorities' discretion).
